2609.12304.title: Hybrid Physics-AI Framework of Body Center of Mass Dynamics from Wrist-Worn Sensors
2609.12304.paper_summary: Wrist-worn IMU has been widely used for daily-life health monitoring. Yet, it does not fully represent whole-body dynamics, for which the body center of mass (COM) is considered the physiological reference standard. Therefore, this work proposes a simplified kinematic model (KM), which is designed to map the wrist IMU to the COM acceleration. It is built upon several reductive assumptions that enable the solvability of the dynamic equations based on wrist IMU measurements alone. This work further proposes three types of hybrid AI modeling methods, namely human kinematic model-based neural network (HKM-NN) models, to leverage the power of both grey-box and black-box modeling. The HKM-NN methods include serial learning (ser-) and two approaches of simultaneous learning (sim1- and sim2-). The proposed models are trained and tested using our dataset, which includes wrist IMU measurements and ground-truth COM measurements from 10 healthy volunteers during six gait activities and sit-to-stand (SS) transitional movement. The results demonstrate the feasibility of estimating COM acceleration from wrist IMU measurements. Our KM model yields satisfactory results, with an error ranging from 6.7% to 12.5% for gait activities and 5.6% for the SS. In comparison with the KM model, our HKM-NN models significantly enhance the performance, achieving 5.3% to 9.3% errors for gait activities, and the best error of 3.9% for the SS. In addition, the HKM-NN models demonstrate distinct robustness characteristics under noisy test conditions, with sim1-/sim2- generally maintaining greater robustness under Gaussian perturbations, while the KM model exhibits comparatively strong robustness under salt-and-pepper noise. These findings highlight the importance of combining biomechanical structure with data-driven learning for wearable sensing applications operating under imperfect and noisy measurement conditions.
2609.12304.paper_summary_zh: 手腕佩戴的慣性測量單元（IMU）已被廣泛應用於日常健康監測。然而，它並不能完全代表全身動力學，因為身體質心（COM）被視為生理參考標準。因此，本研究提出了一個簡化的運動學模型（KM），旨在將手腕IMU映射到COM加速度。該模型基於幾個簡化假設，這使得僅根據手腕IMU測量結果就能解決動力學方程。這項工作進一步提出了三種類型的混合人工智慧建模方法，即基於人類運動學模型的神經網絡（HKM-NN）模型，以利用灰箱和黑箱建模的優勢。HKM-NN方法包括序列學習（ser-）和兩種同時學習的方法（sim1-和sim2-）。所提出的模型使用我們的數據集進行訓練和測試，該數據集包括10名健康志願者在六種步態活動和坐立轉換（SS）運動期間的手腕IMU測量和真實COM測量。結果顯示從手腕IMU測量中估計COM加速度的可行性。我們的KM模型產生了令人滿意的結果，步態活動的誤差範圍為6.7%至12.5%，而SS的誤差為5.6%。與KM模型相比，我們的HKM-NN模型顯著提高了性能，步態活動的誤差達到5.3%至9.3%，而SS的最佳誤差為3.9%。此外，HKM-NN模型在嘈雜測試條件下顯示出明顯的穩健性特徵，其中sim1-/sim2-在高斯擾動下通常保持較大的穩健性，而KM模型在鹽和胡椒噪聲下表現出相對強的穩健性。這些發現突顯了在不完美和嘈雜測量條件下，將生物力學結構與數據驅動學習相結合的重要性，以應用於可穿戴感測技術。
